protocol.description:
A debugging aid: lets a client ask the compositor to record a detailed per-stage timing breakdown of the next N frames on every currently live output, and stream that breakdown back as it's produced.
Not gated behind any permission mechanism (unlike `ironland-capture-permissions-v1`/`ironland-permission-prompt-v1`): nothing here exposes surface contents or other clients' data, only the compositor's own internal timing, so any client may bind this global.

interface.name: ironland_frame_capture_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface allows a client to start frame capture sessions.

request.name: capture
request.description:
Starts a capture session covering every output the compositor currently considers live. `frame_count` frames' worth of timing are reported per output, independently - an output that's asleep or disconnected for the whole session simply never reports any frames rather than blocking the others.
The session ends (see `finished`) once every output live at the time of this request has reported `frame_count` frames, or after a compositor-chosen grace period elapses, whichever comes first.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager doesn't end capture sessions already started through it.

event.name: stage

description.summary: timing for one named stage of one captured frame

event.description: Sent zero or more times per `(output, frame_index)` pair, in the order the stages actually ran, as they're recorded - not necessarily buffered until the whole frame is done. `name` is a short compositor-defined identifier (e.g. "dispatch_clients", "build_elements", "damage_and_draw", "submit"; the udev backend additionally reports "since_vblank" and "vblank_throttled") - not an enum, so new stages can appear without a protocol version bump.

arg.name: start_us
arg.summary: offset from the frame's start, in microseconds

event.name: frame
event.description: Sent once per `(output, frame_index)` pair, after every `stage` event for that frame.

arg.name: stutter
arg.summary: 1 if this frame counted as a stutter, 0 otherwise

event.name: finished
event.description: Sent exactly once, after which no further `stage`/`frame` events follow for this object. The client should destroy it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Ends the session immediately if it's still active. No `finished` event is sent for an explicit destroy.
